rule_text: Issuing authority for BIS Hallmarking Registration (jewellers): Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)
Documents for BIS Hallmarking Registration (jewellers): Business and proprietor details as asked on the NSWS / Manakonline application (the BIS page does not list documents; confirm on the portal)

Fee for BIS Hallmarking Registration (jewellers): BIS charges jewellers no fee for registration (per the BIS jewellers page). Hallmarking of each article is charged separately by the hallmarking centre; confirm current charges with BIS
Apply for BIS Hallmarking Registration (jewellers) on the official portal: https://www.manakonline.in/

BIS Hallmarking Registration (jewellers): Hallmarked gold jewellery must carry the BIS mark, purity in carat and fineness, and a six-digit HUID number. Jewellers apply online for BIS registration through the NSWS portal (reachable via Manakonline). Registration is required in districts where hallmarking is mandatory; confirm for your district.

Expected timeline for BIS Hallmarking Registration (jewellers): BIS states the certificate of registration is granted instantly after the online application and stays valid for life; confirm on the portal
Issuing authority for Bio-Medical Waste Authorisation (State Pollution Control Board): State Pollution Control Board / Pollution Control Committee

Documents for Bio-Medical Waste Authorisation (State Pollution Control Board): Application to the State Pollution Control Board as an occupier under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016 (the exact form and annexures are in the Rules text on the CPCB site)
Fee for Bio-Medical Waste Authorisation (State Pollution Control Board): Not stated in the sources read; confirm with your State Pollution Control Board
Apply for Bio-Medical Waste Authorisation (State Pollution Control Board) on the official portal: https://cpcb.nic.in/rules-3/

Bio-Medical Waste Authorisation (State Pollution Control Board): Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016 every occupier or operator who generates or handles bio-medical waste, irrespective of quantity, must obtain authorisation from the State Pollution Control Board. The Rules cover hospitals, nursing homes, clinics and dispensaries.
Expected timeline for Bio-Medical Waste Authorisation (State Pollution Control Board): Not stated in the sources read; the authorisation carries an expiry date, so plan its renewal

Issuing authority for Clinic / Hospital / Laboratory Registration in Ahmedabad: State or district health authority under your state's clinical-establishment law (the central Act applies only in the states listed by the Health Ministry)

Documents for Clinic / Hospital / Laboratory Registration in Ahmedabad: Documents depend on your state's law. Where the central Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 applies, registration is in two steps: provisional (self-declaration, without inquiry or inspection) and permanent (after category-wise minimum standards are notified); Confirm with your state health department or District Registering Authority which law and forms apply to you
Fee for Clinic / Hospital / Laboratory Registration in Ahmedabad: Not stated in the Health Ministry's FAQ; confirm with your state health authority
Apply for Clinic / Hospital / Laboratory Registration in Ahmedabad on the official portal: https://clinicalestablishments.mohfw.gov.in/faq

Clinic / Hospital / Laboratory Registration in Ahmedabad: The Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 covers hospitals, maternity homes, nursing homes, dispensaries, clinics, sanatoriums and laboratory/diagnostic centres, across all systems of medicine. The Health Ministry's FAQ says it is in force in Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Himachal Pradesh and all Union Territories except Delhi, and in states that adopted it (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Uttarakhand). Elsewhere a state's own law and health authority apply, so check with your state.
Expected timeline for Clinic / Hospital / Laboratory Registration in Ahmedabad: Not stated in the Health Ministry's FAQ; confirm with your state health authority

Issuing authority for Coaching Centre Registration (state rules): State government authority under your state's coaching-centre rules (where notified)

Documents for Coaching Centre Registration (state rules): Registration conditions and documents are set by your state's rules. The Ministry of Education's Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Centres (sent to states on 16 January 2024) cover registration conditions and documents, fees, infrastructure, a code of conduct, student well-being, record keeping and grievance redressal; Publish your fee, easy-exit and fee-refund policy on your website, as the guidelines require
Fee for Coaching Centre Registration (state rules): State-specific; not stated in the sources read
Apply for Coaching Centre Registration (state rules) on the official portal: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2298513&reg=48&lang=2

Coaching Centre Registration (state rules): The Ministry's 2024 guidelines ask states to regulate coaching centres through their own legal framework; some states (for example Rajasthan and Jharkhand in 2025) have passed their own laws. Separately, the Central Consumer Protection Authority's 2024 guidelines on misleading advertisements apply to coaching centres. Confirm what your state requires.
Expected timeline for Coaching Centre Registration (state rules): State-specific; not stated in the sources read
Issuing authority for College / Technical Institution approvals: Affiliating university; AICTE for technical institutions

Documents for College / Technical Institution approvals: For technical institutions (diploma, degree or postgraduate programmes): register and apply for AICTE approval through the NSWS portal, following AICTE's current approval-process handbook and its list of affidavits, certificates and formats; For other colleges: affiliation to a university, under that university's own affiliation rules (not read)
Fee for College / Technical Institution approvals: AICTE sets fees and deadlines for each approval cycle; confirm the current year's notice
Apply for College / Technical Institution approvals on the official portal: https://www.aicte-india.org/bureaus/approval

College / Technical Institution approvals: AICTE's approval process applies to new technical institutions and to added courses or intake at existing ones. Other colleges generally work under an affiliating university. The UGC position and each university's affiliation rules were not read, so an officer will confirm which apply.
Expected timeline for College / Technical Institution approvals: AICTE runs approval in annual cycles with set last dates; check the current cycle
Issuing authority for Retail Drug (Pharmacy) Licence in Ahmedabad: State Drugs Control Department (State Licensing Authority under the Drugs Rules, 1945)

Documents for Retail Drug (Pharmacy) Licence in Ahmedabad: Application in Form 19 (as used in the Delhi checklist; confirm your state's system and form); Site plan of the premises and proof of premises (ownership or rent agreement); Proof of constitution of the firm and photo ID of the proprietor / partners / directors; Affidavit of non-conviction under the Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940; Registered Pharmacist: qualification certificates, state pharmacy council registration and appointment letter; Premises: an independent shop of at least 10 sq m (15 sq m if both Form 20/21 and 20B/21B are sought); This list is based on the Delhi Drugs Control Department's official checklist; your state's checklist may differ in details, so confirm it with your State Drugs Control Department

Fee for Retail Drug (Pharmacy) Licence in Ahmedabad: The amount is not stated in the checklist that was read; the fee is paid online or by challan with the application. Confirm it with your State Drugs Control Department
Apply for Retail Drug (Pharmacy) Licence in Ahmedabad on the official portal: https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/resources/UploadCDSCOWeb/2022/drug_rules/Drugs%20Rules,%201945.pdf

Retail Drug (Pharmacy) Licence in Ahmedabad: Retail sale of drugs needs a licence from the State Licensing Authority under the Drugs Rules, 1945: Form 20 (allopathic drugs outside Schedules C, C(1) and X), Form 21 (Schedule C and C(1) drugs, excluding Schedule X) and Form 20F (Schedule X). A registered pharmacist (or another competent person the Rules allow) must be in charge of the premises.

Documents for Retail Drug (Pharmacy) Licence in Delhi: System-generated online fee deposit receipt(s); System-generated application in Form 19 / 19C, as applicable; System-generated self-declaration of the proprietor / partners / directors; Site plan and key plan of the premises; Proof of constitution of the firm (proprietorship declaration; partnership deed with list of partners; LLP deed and ROC certificate; memorandum, articles, ROC certificate and board resolution for a company; trust deed; society by-laws; HUF deed); Photo ID proof of the proprietor / partner / director; Affidavit of non-conviction of the proprietor / partner / director and the firm under the Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940; Affidavit of compliance with the Delhi Master Plan (MPD-2021) for the type of premises; Receipt of applicable charges (such as registration or conversion charges) issued by MCD, with documents supporting commercial use; Registered Pharmacist (technical person): Aadhaar, self-declaration, qualification certificates and mark sheets, valid Delhi Pharmacy Council registration, appointment letter, bio-data in the prescribed format; Premises: registered sale deed / GPA / conveyance deed (or unregistered ones with electricity bill, water bill or property tax receipt); if rented, rent receipt and rent agreement with the landlord's ownership documents; Premises must be an independent shop of at least 10 sq m (15 sq m for both Form 20/21 and 20B/21B), with clear height per the National Building Code; All documents are to be self-attested; no drug licence is granted in a residential plot or flat unless MPD-2021 allows it
